name: Kumāralāta
dates_notes: Usually placed in the second or third century CE; the chronology is inferred from later Buddhist reports and is not fixed by a dated autograph or inscription.
core_thesis: Kumāralāta is a major early voice associated with the Dārṣṭāntika and later Sautrāntika current. The surviving material chiefly shows a literary and pedagogical use of illustrative narratives; it does not support a full reconstruction of a discrete doctrinal system or a secure genealogy for later Sautrāntikas.

engaged_works.title: Kalpanamanditika
engaged_works.ascription_notes: The work is attributed to Kumāralāta in the manuscript and later transmission. It survives only in Sanskrit fragments and in non-Indic witnesses; its original scope and exact title remain uncertain.
engaged_works.summary: A collection of didactic narratives and illustrations preserved fragmentarily in Sanskrit and through Tibetan, Chinese, and other Central Asian transmission. It provides direct but incomplete evidence for Kumāralāta's literary method; it is not a complete philosophical treatise.

reception_notes: Later doxography associates Kumāralāta with Sautrāntika formation. That association is historically important but should be distinguished from the fragmentary evidence of the surviving work.
